title: separate-fastpath-lint-tiers-and-add-dep-safelisting
author: Priya Desai
description: Context: Our presubmit pipeline runs a monolithic linter and a broad dependency upgrade scanner which has been adding latency to author feedback loops and producing noisy dependency PRs. This change splits the presubmit linting into three fast-tiered lanes (fastpath, standard, heavy) and introduces a lightweight dependency safelisting component that quarantines known-flaky devdeps and promotes low-risk dependency bumps to a fast approval path. Motivation: reduce median presubmit latency for code changes (target < 60s for shallow edits), lower noise from dependency churn, and make it easier to roll out targeted linter updates without impacting the whole repo. What this PR does: - Adds a presubmit manifest that maps changed paths to lint tiers (fastpath covers docs, small TS/py edits; standard runs common linters; heavy runs expensive static analyzers and typecheck on larger touch areas). - Introduces a minimal Go-based presubmit agent (ci/cmd/presubmit-router) that reads the manifest, sets workflow inputs, and tags PRs with the chosen tier. - Adds tools/dep-safelister to maintain an allowlist of devdeps that may be auto-approved for minor versions and a quarantine list for flaky packages. - Refactors .github/workflows/presubmit.yml into three composite jobs and a router step that routes to the appropriate lane. - Documentation: docs/presubmit.md describes the tiering rules, signals for escalation, and how to add packages to the safelist. Rollout plan: staged rollout on the repo: 1) deploy presubmit-router in dry-run mode for two weeks, 2) enable fastpath routing for docs and small edits, 3) opt-in standard/heavy lanes for teams, 4) start auto-approving low-risk dep bumps after monitoring. Checklist (author): [x] manifests and tests for tier mapping, [x] unit tests for dep-safelister, [x] end-to-end smoke run in ephemeral branch, [x] docs updated. Checklist (ops): [x] add router to allowed workflows in org policies, [x] prepare rollback (revert to single presubmit workflow). Commits (high-level): see commits field for messages. Changed areas (high level): .github/workflows/presubmit.yml, ci/presubmit/router.go (new), tools/dep-safelister/{main.go,policy.yaml}, scripts/bootstrap-presubmit.sh (reworked), docs/presubmit.md, tests/presubmit/tier-mapping.test.yaml. Testing performed: - Local unit tests for router and safelister (go test). - Full presubmit simulation on a fork with 120 synthetic PRs covering docs, small code, and large refactors. - Canary: enabled fastpath for the docs team for 48 hours, observed median queue time drop from 110s to 47s. Risks and mitigations: - Misclassification could under-run heavy linters: router defaults to next-higher tier when path heuristics are ambiguous. - Auto-approve of dep bumps could surface supply-chain risk: safelist only targets devdeps and minor semver bumps; release notes require manual review for prod deps. Related: ENG-4582 presubmit performance sprint; ENG-4620 dep hygiene initiative. Merge: squash merge after reviewer approvals.

review_comments: Alexei Morozov: Can we make the router heuristics deterministic by adding a path-weight table? Response: added a tier priority table and unit tests (see tests/presubmit/tier-mapping.test.yaml).

Jordan Kim: Dep safelist seems powerful — how do we revoke an entry? Response: policy.yaml includes a revocation window and safelist entries require 2 approvers from infra. Added documentation in docs/presubmit.md.

Samira Patel: CI flakes in heavy lane might still block merges. Suggest adding an auto-fallback to rerun heavy jobs as separate nightlies. Response: agreed; added fallback to nightly heavy-linting job and a note in the rollout plan.
release_notes: Introduce tiered presubmit linting (fastpath/standard/heavy) to reduce author wait time and add a dev dependency safelister to reduce noisy dep PRs. No user-facing changes. Ops: follow rollout steps in docs/presubmit.md.
